newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM tells parliament more floods possible.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM tells parliament more floods possible.

text.p: Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz warned parliament on Thursday that weather forecasts showed heavy rain overnight may cause a new wave of floods in the country's south.

"We must expect the possiblity, unfortunately, of the start of another wave of floods," he told an emergency session of parliament called to deal with the disastrous effects of floods caused by rain last week.

Cimoszewicz said at the start of Thursday's parliamentary debate that meteorological services of Poland and three other countries has said that 70 mms of rain could fall over the neighbouring Czech Republic during 12 hours which could flow into Poland.

On Friday in western and north western Poland there could be 50 mms of rain in 12 hours and 70 mms overnight from Friday to Saturday, he said, adding that forecasters said their predictions were 90 percent likely to prove correct.

The prime minister said that as levels in rivers were still high and there was not much capacity in reservoirs, there was not much scope to absorb the additional water. He added that the news could affect parliament decisions on flood relief and "and also on the safety of people".

Police put the death toll in Poland by late Wednesday at 46 in the last wave of floods which began with downpours early last week. Water has swamped 4,500 sq km (1,700 square miles), of which around two-fifths was still inundated. It has struck 40,000 farms, 86 towns and 875 villages.
